Per-variant majority for haplotype A (alt cluster):
- Most variants: alt=1 on hap A. R009=1,R023=1,R025=0→ uncertain); V049 only one read (0)→ set 0.

answer.method_summary: I clustered the 25 reads into two anti-correlated haplotype groups by their overlapping allele patterns. One group (R001, R002, R005, R008, R009, R011, R013, R018, R023, R025) predominantly carries alternate alleles across the variant set; the complementary group (R003, R004, R006, R007, R012, R016, R017, R019, R024, etc.) carries reference alleles at the same positions. Haplotype A was defined as the alt-carrying haplotype and each variant's A-allele was resolved by weighted majority vote over reads assigned to that cluster, minimizing per-read mismatches (a MEC-style objective). Most variants are called with strong consensus (single dissenting read out of many). V002 is consistently reference on the alt-haplotype (a real het where alt phases to hap B). V045, V048, and V049 phase to reference on hap A based on the reads spanning the far-right block (R009/R023/R025/R024). Variants flagged uncertain (V020, V027, V030, V036, V039, V045, V048, V049) had conflicting long-read calls consistent with PacBio error and thinner coverage near block boundaries; their majority call was retained but confidence is lower. Haplotype B is the exact complement of every reported allele. The global A/B swap is scored equivalently.
